entities.name: 'machine learning'
entities.criterion: A passage uses "machine learning" (or the adjectival "machine-learning") for learning by computing machines or programs, as a name for a subject, method or field; uses for learning to operate a machine are another sense.

search.venues: Crossref index (bibliographic query "machine learning", publication dates 1940 to 1959, 200 rows by relevance, titles screened for the phrase); the Dartmouth proposal (1955) in the 1996 HTML transcription; Samuel (1959) in a later reprint; Minsky (1961) in the dataset transcription. Turing (1950) is in the dataset only as a scan without a text layer and was not searched.
search.years: 1936–1961 for the earliest-located question; later uses recorded only where a retrieved text of this group already contained the term.
search.methods: Full-text search of the retrieved texts; screening of Crossref titles for "machine learning" and "learning machine"; reading of the index records for the earliest hits.
search.gaps: Only titles and metadata are searched in Crossref, not full texts; Google Books, HathiTrust and the Internet Archive full-text search were not used. 1950s conference proceedings outside Crossref (for example IRE convention records) were not searched. The pre-1959 texts of Samuel, Friedberg ("A Learning Machine", IBM Journal 1958) and Selfridge were not read.
search.failures: Campaigne (1959) text: ACM Digital Library HTTP 403 (dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/1457838.1457868 and the landing page); Semantic Scholar has no abstract. Samuel (1959) on IEEE Xplore not attempted (the index link is the IEEE host, which refuses automated retrieval in earlier packs).

corrections.reason: Same-family audit: Campaigne’s paper (Western Joint Computer Conference, 3–5 March 1959) is known here only from its title as indexed by Crossref; its text was not read (ACM refused), so its sense is unverified. Its text decides the role; if it does not meet the criterion, the earliest located text read is Samuel (IBM Journal, July 1959).

entities.note: The earliest-located role rests on a title read in an index record (Campaigne, March 1959), with the sense inferred from the venue; the earliest text read in full is Samuel (July 1959). See openQuestions.

withheld.reason: Campaigne’s paper (Western Joint Computer Conference, 3–5 March 1959) is known here only from its title as indexed by Crossref; its text was not read (ACM refused), so its sense is unverified. Its text decides the role; if it does not meet the criterion, the earliest located text read is Samuel (IBM Journal, July 1959).

entities.name: Probabilistic and Bayesian methods
entities.criterion: A passage names an approach to machine inference, decision or reasoning as Bayesian or probabilistic (for example "Bayes nets", "Bayesian networks", "Bayes inference"); for a definition, it states what the approach does with probabilities.

search.venues: Minsky (1961, dataset transcription); AAAI-82 proceedings (Pearl); UCLA technical reports (Pearl 1985, two versions); IJCAI-85 proceedings (Cheeseman); Crossref index (bibliographic query "bayesian inference artificial intelligence machine", to 1984, 60 rows).
search.methods: Full-text search of the retrieved texts for "Bayes"; reading of the report covers and abstracts from page images where there is no text layer; screening of Crossref titles.
search.gaps: Duda, Hart and Nilsson, "Subjective Bayesian methods for rule-based inference systems" (AFIPS 1976; reprinted 1981) was found in the index but not retrieved; Pearl's 1988 book and 1950s–1960s pattern-recognition literature (for example Chow 1957) were not searched. The Dartmouth proposal and Samuel (1959) do not use "Bayes".
search.failures: Semantic Scholar API: HTTP 429 for the Duda, Hart and Nilsson search.

entities.note: Minsky's "Bayes nets" (1961) and Pearl's "Bayesian networks" (1985) are recorded side by side; the pack shows no transmission between them.

entities.name: Evolutionary computation
entities.criterion: A passage names, as a method of computation or optimisation, a procedure modelled on biological evolution (variation and selection in a population), under a name such as evolutionary programming, evolution strategy, genetic algorithm, simulated evolution or evolutionary computation.

search.venues: Crossref index (bibliographic queries "genetic algorithm", "simulated evolution", "evolutionary programming", "evolution strategy", publication dates to 1980, 100 rows each, titles screened); Crossref journal listing for Evolutionary Computation (ISSN 1063-6560), 1993; Koza (1990 report); Minsky (1961).
search.methods: Title screening of index results; full-text search of the retrieved texts.
search.gaps: The texts most often cited for the family's early history were not retrieved: Friedberg (IBM Journal 1958), Holland (J. ACM 1962; book 1975), Fogel, Owens and Walsh (book 1966), Bagley (thesis 1967), Rechenberg (1965 report; 1973 book), De Jong (thesis 1975). The "genetic algorithm" query returned only items with incorrect dates (1970-01-01 placeholders for recent papers); "simulated evolution" returned no matching title. The earliest located record is therefore an index title and is likely to be displaced by a fuller search.
search.failures: ACM Digital Library HTTP 403 (Holland 1962, dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/321127.321128); University of Michigan Deep Blue HTTP 403 and an empty bitstream page (De Jong 1975, deepblue.lib.umich.edu/handle/2027.42/4507); MIT Press direct.mit.edu browser challenge, HTTP 403 (Bäck and Schwefel 1993).

entities.name: Reinforcement learning
entities.criterion: A passage names learning by a machine from reward or reinforcement signals as "reinforcement learning" (or a "reinforcement learning device/system"); for a definition, it states how actions or predictions are adjusted from reward.

search.venues: Dartmouth proposal (1996 transcription); Samuel (1959 reprint); Minsky (1961); Sutton (1988); Watkins (1989, page images of title page and preface only); Tesauro (1995); Sutton and Barto (2018), section 1.7 and chapter notes.
search.years: 1955–1995, with the 2018 history for attributed statements.
search.methods: Full-text search for "reinforcement learning" and "reinforcement"; citation following from Sutton and Barto's history.
search.gaps: Minsky's 1954 Princeton dissertation and the 1960s engineering literature named by Sutton and Barto (Waltz and Fu 1965; Mendel 1966) were not retrieved. Watkins's thesis has no text layer and was not searched beyond its first pages.
search.failures: None for the texts listed; see the evolutionary and statistical-learning blocks for refusals by shared hosts.

openQuestions.question: Should the earliest-located role for 'machine learning' rest on Campaigne's March 1959 conference title, read only in index records with the sense inferred from the venue, or on Samuel (July 1959), the earliest text read in full?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep Campaigne as the earliest located (inferred, flagged) and ask the cross-family checker to try the ACM text; if the text cannot be read before admission, admit Campaigne as earliest located with its inference stated, and keep Samuel as a use. If the maintainer prefers a rule that the headline must rest on a text read in full, swap the roles and record the swap as a correction.

openQuestions.question: The same index-title rule decides the evolutionary (Burgin 1973) and support-vector (Cortes and Vapnik 1995) headlines. Is a title read in a publisher-deposited index record enough for an earliest-located headline?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes for admission as a candidate, with derivation inferred where the sense is not self-evident, but mark both families' searches as weak; the evolutionary headline in particular is likely to be displaced by the 1958–1967 texts if a later pass retrieves them.

openQuestions.question: The dataset already has the concept `reinforcement-learning`. Should the family use that ID instead of `th-fam-reinforcement-learning`?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes: map th-fam-reinforcement-learning to the existing `reinforcement-learning` concept at merge or admission, keeping this group's criterion and search note on it.

openQuestions.question: Sutton and Barto say "reinforcement learning" was first used in the engineering literature in the 1960s; Minsky (1961) uses "reinforcement learning device". Contested?
openQuestions.recommended: No: both are recorded as supported statements of what each text says; the book's statement is about the engineering literature and does not directly deny Minsky's use. Leave them side by side.

openQuestions.question: Should Valiant (1984) be under statistical learning, or under a separate learning-theory heading?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it under th-fam-statistical-learning with the qualification already given; the scope has no separate learning-theory family.
